summary: Jiryo Masuda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Unrai Wogihara (attested 1930). Masuda served as a professor at the University of Calcutta and taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.
Jishu Oda (1908–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as rector of Choboji Monastery (attested 1914) and was an emeritus professor at Shuchiin University (attested 1977).

Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendra Nath Mohanty (1928–2023) studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1952–1954). In philosophy and Indology, he held teaching posts at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, Oklahoma, Emory, and Temple University.
Jitsushyu Oshika (born 1919) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Oshika studied at Tohoku University and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

Jitsuzo Kuwabara (1871–1931) was a sinologist and historian. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1896), he held posts at the Third Higher School (1898–1899), Tokyo Higher Normal School (1899–1907), and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota (born 1932) is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Kubota studied under traditional teacher Yamada Koun from approximately 1970 to 1989 and later succeeded him.

Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He. Active in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Ren taught at Peking University and directed the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and National Library of China.

Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) studied at Durham University, Trinity Laban Conservatoire, and Soji-ji, training under several traditional teachers. A Buddhist and religious studies figure, she was head priest at Unpuku-ji (~1968–1969) and abbess of Shasta Abbey (~1970–1996).

Joachim Gentz specializes in sinology and religious studies. He has held positions as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).
Joachim Heinrich Campe (1746–1818) was a linguist who studied at the University of Helmstedt (~1765) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1765–1768). He taught Wilhelm von Humboldt.
Joachim Prandstetter specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned a Magister degree at the University of Vienna by 1994, studying under Gerhard Oberhammer (attested 1994).

Joachim Wach (1898–1955) studied at Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, Leiden, Leipzig (Dissertation 1917–1922), and Heidelberg. A scholar of religious studies and philosophy, he taught at Leipzig, Brown, and the University of Chicago.

Joan Jiko Halifax (born 1942) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Tulane, Newcomb, Miami, and Union Institute & University (PhD), and held posts at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Miami, Harvard, and Library of Congress.

Joanna Gottfried Williams (1939–2022) studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (1960–1969). A specialist in Indology and history/archaeology, she was a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1971 to 2003.

Joanna Macy (1929–2025) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at Wellesley College (~1946–1950) and Syracuse University (~1973–1978), and she taught Stephanie Kaza and Doug Kraft.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne, educated at the University of Chicago, is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She held posts at University of Massachusetts Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

Joe Bransford Wilson, a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, earned a Ph.D. from the University of Virginia (1984) and studied at UW–Madison. He taught at Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb (born 1947) studied at Queen Mary University of London and University of London. Working in numismatics, archaeology, and Indology, he held posts at the British Museum (1970–2010), Royal Numismatic Society, Oriental Numismatic Society, and Hebei Normal University.

Joel Peter Brereton (born 1948) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Stanley Insler in 1971. He held academic posts at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin (2004).
